component.name: Pereplyot
component.summary: Standalone PDF and EPUB reader with annotations

description.p: Pereplyot (переплёт — Russian for "binding") is a standalone PDF and EPUB reader: highlight, underline, strike, and leave freestanding notes, with full-text search, continuous scroll, and resumed reading position. No vault to set up — just open a file.
Features:

ul.li: Open a PDF or EPUB by file picker, drag-and-drop, or "Open With".
Highlights, underlines, strikes, notes, and bookmarks, marked from a popover that appears when you select text.
Export your notes as Typst, LaTeX or Markdown, grouped by what each highlight colour means, with citations.
A Text view for PDFs that screen readers can read and the keyboard can select.
In-document search, continuous scroll, facing-pages view, and zoom-to-fit for PDFs.
Rotate and invert-colours (night reading) for PDF; Light/Sepia/Dark reading themes and font choice for EPUB.
A page-thumbnail grid, click-to-turn page zones, and keyboard/mouse page and chapter navigation.
Reading position and annotations remembered per document automatically.
A Notebook (a plain Typst file) beside the reading, with quotes you drag in from your notes, connections between annotations, and export with citations.
Search across the text of everything you have read and every note, with filters.
EPUB printed page numbers, note popovers, a paginated mode, and clipped images.
A Library with named shelves for documents you keep, separate from History's record of everything you've opened, and a Notes tab that searches every annotation.

description.p: 0.21.0 "Open Folio" — with a notebook open beside the document, every new highlight, underline, strike-out, clipped area and note on a selection is added to it as a cited quote, in the PDF and EPUB readers; a toggle in the notebook's menu turns it off.

0.20.2 "Facing Leaf" — in Two-page view you can now select, highlight, underline, clip and right-click on the right-hand page of a spread, not just the left; the hover preview of links and citations works on both.
0.20.1 "Clean Gutter" — selecting text on a multi-column PDF page now follows one column and then the next instead of cutting across the gutter, for dragging and for clipping a rectangle.

0.20.0 "Fair Copy" — scanned PDFs are recognised in the background as soon as they open, the page in view first, and their text can be selected, copied, highlighted and clipped in the normal page view as well as in Reading mode. Selecting by dragging no longer breaks off after a letter or a line in EPUBs or in Reading mode. Add to Library and Add to Kartoteka are in the ⋮ menu of both readers.

0.19.0 "Kettle Stitch" — notes you can't lose: changes made to a document's notes in another window or app are kept instead of overwritten, earlier versions of each document's notes are kept and can be restored, and a daily backup can copy everything to a folder you choose.

0.18.0 "Loose Leaf" — Pereplyot can hand a document's text to other apps: --extract-text prints a PDF's or EPUB's text without opening a window, and the flatpak installs it as the pereplyot-extract-text command. Sputnik uses it to read PDF syllabi.

0.17.2 "Mended Spine" — a password-protected PDF keeps its outline and page numbers and its unlocked copy is deleted when you close the tab, dialogs follow a tab dragged into another window, and Reading mode no longer widens the window.
0.17.1 "Steady Page" — Reading mode stops freezing a long book while it loads and at the first click, and its page counter and chapter now follow your scrolling.

0.17.0 "Turned Key" — password-protected PDFs open (Pereplyot asks for the password and reads an unlocked copy kept in its cache for a day), and a tab dragged out of the tab bar becomes its own window instead of snapping back.

0.16.3 "Quiet Hands" — the Markdown notes folder is written on a background thread, so editing never waits for the disk or a synced folder, and the file left behind when a document is renamed is removed.

0.16.2 "Closed Door" — fixes a crash a crafted pereplyot:// link could cause (a percent sign followed by a non-ASCII character), the same slip in the EPUB link reader, and a notebook line that could crash the notebook loader. The text parsers are now fuzzed with tens of thousands of hostile inputs.

0.16.1 "Light Load" — big EPUBs unpack in the background instead of freezing the window, and the notes sidebars build 300 cards at a time with a "Show more" row, so a book with thousands of marks opens at once.

0.16.0 "Narrow Margin" — the EPUB reader no longer needs a very wide window (secondary controls moved into a menu, long chapter titles shorten), Add to Library is a command in each reader's palette, a wrong value in one setting no longer resets the rest and a damaged settings file is set aside, History moves into the data folder, opening a large file no longer freezes the window, and a few smaller messages and checks were tightened.

0.15.1 "Tight Binding" — a hardening release after an adversarial test pass. Fixes a crash in Reading mode on scans with broken coordinates; stops EPUBs reaching the network or starting the browser unprompted; makes Open With work for several files and for relative paths; keeps a longer History and sets a damaged one aside; stops the Markdown notes folder overwriting files that are not its own; makes library thumbnails render in the background; and adds Ctrl+W and Ctrl+1 for tabs.

0.15.0 "Common Room" — the library is now the first tab of the reader window, pinned and always visible, instead of a separate window that gets lost behind the reader. Opening a book adds a tab beside it, and closing the last one returns you to the library. Also fixes a crash when adding a document to the Library from History, and keeps a book's place when you switch tabs and back.

0.14.0 "Quiet Page" — Reading mode copes with scanned books: footnote markers the scan mangled are matched to their notes, endnotes gathered at the back are placed beside the text that cites them, running heads stay out of the text, and the cover and title pages are kept as pictures that Select All leaves out. The page-colours button now works in Reading mode and sets one theme for PDFs and EPUBs, EPUBs gain the button, and the line-spacing slider reaches single spacing.

0.13.0 "Loose Leaf" — notes can leave the app: an optional Markdown notes folder keeps one file per document, with a stable block id on each highlight, for Obsidian or Logseq, and "Add to Kartoteka" hands the open file to Kartoteka 0.22. Search results open with the hit marked and recognised scans are searched; OCR languages are ones you add yourself. Areas resize by their corners, notes show in Reading mode, paginated EPUBs turn with a click at the edges, notebook export includes clipped EPUB pictures, and merging marks undoes in one step.

0.12.0 "Clear Margin" — a Ctrl+K command palette in the readers and the launcher, caret browsing (F7) to select and mark on the page from the keyboard alone, optional textures on highlights so the four colours can be told apart without colour, a Welcome / What's New window, EPUB covers on Library cards and a new app icon. Fixes printed page numbers for EPUBs that list their pages only in the navigation file.

0.11.0 "Gilt Spine" — a Notebook beside your reading, with quotes that open their passage and export to Typst, Markdown or LaTeX with citations. Search the text of everything you have read and all your notes at once. EPUBs get printed page numbers, note popovers, a paginated mode and clipped images. Reading mode re-sets a PDF as clean text in Zerkalo's LaTeX Look, with Tesseract OCR for scans. Area capture, links that open a passage, marks imported from other readers, and a much faster renderer.

0.10.0 "Fair Copy" — export notes as Typst, LaTeX or Markdown grouped by colour meaning, with citations. Select text first, then mark it from a popover. Library shelves, adjustable card size, and a Notes tab that searches every annotation. A Text view for PDFs usable with a screen reader or keyboard alone, working PDF links, OCR for scanned PDFs, and much safer saving. Large PDFs use a fraction of the memory.

0.9.0 "True Register" — fixed PDF selection and highlighting missing the text under the pointer on many publisher and scanned PDFs. Copied and saved text now keeps its spaces, a right-click copies selected or highlighted text, and keyboard page navigation works from anywhere in the reader window.

0.8.0 "Open Clasp" — Kartoteka's Annotations window now opens in Pereplyot, and documents opened from Kartoteka or Sputnik show their library title. Fixed Pereplyot staying open in the background after its reader was closed, when launched from another app or a file manager.

0.7.0 "Ochre Thread" — highlighting now uses a four-colour reading scheme shown right in the toolbar: warm ochre for key ideas, dusty blue for evidence, sage for connections, and terracotta for problems and questions. Each colour's label can be renamed from the menu. Two-page and Continuous views are now compact icon toggles.

0.6.0 "Wide Margin" — notes and highlights reworked to match how other readers handle them: margin notes are no longer limited to a single line, every annotation list now shows its highlight color, the Annotations dialog shows the quoted passage instead of just its location, and that dialog gained a search field.

0.5.0 "Turned Leaf" — page thumbnails moved into the Contents sidebar as a second tab alongside Outline, instead of a separate popup window. Fixed a real bug where reopening a document showed the right page number but the wrong page content, always landing back on page 1 instead of resuming where you left off.

0.4.1 "Slim Gutter" — both readers' chrome is consolidated down to one header row and one status-bar row per tab, instead of two header rows and (for the PDF reader) three bottom rows, leaving more of the window for the document itself. The PDF reader's search bar and the reader window's version/changelog button both moved into its status bar. Also fixes the Contents sidebar toggle's icon sometimes rendering as a generic "missing icon" glyph in icon themes without `sidebar-show-symbolic` under that exact name.

0.4.0 "Shared Binding" — Kartoteka and Sputnik now launch this app directly to open a document, instead of each embedding an aging pinned copy of the reader. New command-line modes route annotations, reading position, and the page-numbering override straight into Kartoteka's vault or Sputnik's course-material store, so opening a citation or material from either app behaves exactly as it always has — just with this app's reader instead of a stale embedded one. Also fixes a bug where closing the reader via its window's own close button (rather than an explicit tab-close) silently never saved your reading position.

0.3.0 "Folded Corner" — bookmarks, PDF rotate and invert-colours (night reading), a page-thumbnail grid and click-to-turn page zones, EPUB reading themes (Light/ Sepia/Dark) and font choice, reading-progress percentages, and Markdown export of notes and highlights. Also adds fullscreen/maximize buttons, a version/changelog button on the reader window itself, and fixes the Contents toggle disappearing for documents with no outline/table of contents.

0.2.0 "Shared Shelf" — History is now shared across every app that embeds the reader: opening a document from Kartoteka or Sputnik shows up in Pereplyot's History too. Also fixes Pereplyot sometimes failing to fully close when opened purely to view one file from another app.

0.1.1 "True Margin" — a duplicate "Reader" title, keyboard page navigation that never actually fired, and a misplaced Notes sidebar toggle, all fixed; hamburger menu and status bar now match the rest of the suite.

0.1.0 "Quiet Spine" — first release: a standalone PDF/EPUB reader built around the same reader widget Kartoteka and Sputnik embed, with a Library/History shelf, zoom-to-fit, and keyboard page navigation.
